# NOTES: TWO BOOKS

## BOOK 1: THE CLOCK STRUCK ONE (Fergus Hume, 1898, Frederick Warne; "Boston-Library Society" scan)

**Cast**
- **Dora Carew**: 21, ward of Edermont, tall, gold curls, gray eyes, aquiline nose, sunburnt, bicycle; "modern Diana on a bicycle." Fiancée of Allen Scott. Believes she has £500/yr from parents (false).
- **Dr Allen Scott**: young doctor, Canterbury (green-doored house near Cathedral). Son of late Dr Scott (died ~20 yrs ago, when Allen was 5; mother died at his birth). Haggard, guilt-ridden later.
- **Julian Edermont** (real name **Julian Dargill**): recluse, Red House, Chillum, near Canterbury, ~20 yrs there. Small, noble white head, silvery beard, cowardly; obsessed with Litany prayer "From battle and murder, and from sudden death, good Lord, deliver us." Locks house, gates, postern, kitchen.
- **Lambert Joad**: ~60, Edermont's Oxford/college friend, failed Anglican parson, drunk, bluish-red face, watery pale-blue eyes, rusty black, white ribbon collar, carpet slippers, flask of brandy; lusts after Dora. Sleeps in cottage across road from 9pm to 9am.
- **Meg Gance**: cook/general servant, locked in kitchen at night; stout, "Lor'," dialect.
- **Mrs Tice**: Allen's old nurse, now housekeeper; large, motherly, guards secret.
- **Mr Carver**: Canterbury lawyer, lean, dry, misogynist, office near Mercery Lane.
- **Lady Laura Burville** (born Laura Treherne; also Mrs Carew, Mrs Dargill): small, frail, doll-like, golden hair, white tea-gown; frivolous, selfish; guest of Sir Harry Hernwood at Hernwood Hall; lives 22 Jersey Place, Mayfair. Husband **Sir John Burville** (African millionaire, burly, violent temper, portrait).
- **Augustus Pallant**: red hair, blue eyes, supercilious, gambler, blackmailer; "Beware of Allen Scott!"; later shot in San Francisco over fan-tan.
- **Mr Pride** (= **John Mallison**): chubby, silver-haired, tutor at Chillum school, resembles Edermont; murderer.
- **Inspector Jedd**: Canterbury, pompous, theory = tramp/burglar.
- **Dr Chambers**: Canterbury medical witness.
- **Sir Harry Hernwood**: dapper, mincing fool; gives Lady Burville's address.
- **Captain George Theophilus Carew**: Dora's father, sea captain (ship *Silver Arrow*), violent; "died" in Guinea, actually escaped, later drunk gambler, died San Francisco (in Pallant's arms).
- **Dr Scott** (Allen's father): shot dead by Carew (mistaken for Dargill) ~20 yrs ago at Christchurch, Hants.
- **John Mallison**: Dargill's friend; took Dargill's name to lure Carew to America.

**Chronology**
- **Ch I** (July noon): Dora on bicycle at bridge 2 mi from Canterbury. Meets Allen. Allen was called to Lady Burville (fainted in church Sunday). Edermont also fainted in Chillum Church at Litany. Allen: Lady Burville "looks like a doll, talks like a fool." Gates/postern locked. Joad, Pride mentioned.
- **Ch II**: Joad admits knowing Allen's father; hints Lady Burville knew him. Edermont from window: "Come upstairs, Allen." Edermont shrieks "Lambert! ... He will kill me!" Allen flees: "Don't stop me, for God's sake!"
- **Ch III**: Edermont: "Because of your parents ... their sin will be visited on you." Warns of Lady Burville ("evil woman"). Allen promised silence. Joad: "This is the beginning of the end." Hall clock 2:30pm.
- **Ch IV**: Mrs Tice: Allen left for London (train from Selling, 4.26). Shows portrait of young clean-shaven Edermont. "You will never become the wife of Allen Scott."
- **Ch V**: Week passes. Study: oak-panelled, off hall; drawing-room off study with glass door to laurel hedge. Pallant calls "on behalf of Laura Burville." Edermont: "My nightmare is at an end!" then faints.
- **Ch VI**: Pallant: "Beware of Allen Scott!" Allen's letter: returns 2 Aug. Edermont wrote Allen (late July, posted himself) and a third letter. Night of 2 Aug: Edermont tells Dora to go to bed. Dora hears cry, clock strikes one. Morning (3 Aug): Meg: "bashed in like a pumpkin!"
- **Ch VII**: Study: bureau smashed, Zulu knobkerrie, pistol, papers scattered. Joad arrives before 8, finds postern and side door open. Dora sends for police. Allen arrives with doctor; says he will end engagement; Dora refuses release: "you are my affianced husband."
- **Ch VIII**: Inquest (dining-room). Witnesses: Meg, Dora (time = before the one o'clock strike), Joad (with Pride till after 2am), Dr Chambers (death 12–1am), Jedd. Verdict: murder by person(s) unknown. Edermont buried Chillum churchyard. Will read by Carver: Red House, pictures, silver, £200/yr (three farms) to Dora on condition she stays in Red House and keeps Joad; £50,000 unconditional to whoever punishes assassin; life story sealed in bureau.
- **Ch IX**: *Morning Planet* leader. Carver: no £500 income, no parent evidence; Edermont bought Red House 20 yrs ago, Dora a babe. Dora estimated £8,000 saved (false). Carver: "find that woman."
- **Ch X**: Dora visits Allen; he refuses explanation; Joad admires her; Allen threatens Joad. Dora asks for Mrs Tice to stay at Red House.
- **Ch XI**: Mrs Tice moves in. Dora trick: says Christchurch; Mrs Tice slips "Edermont is a false name." Mrs Tice's husband buried Christchurch Priory. Mrs Tice: "rat of a man," not his lover.
- **Ch XII**: Dora flatters Joad. Joad drunk: "I forced him [Edermont]." Dora: "Did you kill Mr Edermont?" Joad: not him; claims he knows who did. Proposes marriage; "Allen Scott, the murderer!"
- **Ch XIII**: Joad's evidence: ~midnight saw Allen on bicycle near Red House postern; Joad with Pride from ~2am. Joad gives Dora a week. Dora to Canterbury; Allen: "I was mad on that night."
- **Ch XIV**: Allen: Edermont's letter asked midnight meeting, postern open. He rode wildly, reached Red House ~1am; found Edermont dead; candle died; fled. Met woman cyclist (on way in, and again at railway bridge, puncture; he mended tyre). Found pearl brooch "L.B." in study.
- **Ch XV**: Dora gets Lady Burville's address from Sir Harry (pretext: found brooch). No. 22 Jersey Place, Mayfair.
- **Ch XVI**: Dora to London by train from Selling; Pride in same compartment (says he met man and woman on bicycles, walked from Canterbury to Chillum past 1am). Lady Burville: "I am your mother."
- **Ch XVII**: Lady Burville's story: married Capt. Carew (sea captain); "widowed" after 6 months; married Dargill ~1 yr later (Dargill rich); Dora born; Carew returned alive; Dargill fled to America; returned, paid annuity for Dora; Laura accepted. Pallant (from America ~2 yrs ago) blackmails over bigamy. Laura married Sir John. Dargill sent note; Laura visited Red House at night and collected letters. Laura: "George Carew killed Mr Dargill." Extracts silence promise.
- **Ch XVIII**: Dora returns ~8pm; Joad at gate: "She'll have to marry me." Mrs Tice angry. Next morning Pallant calls: met Carew in San Francisco; Carew "died in my arms." Edermont's "enemy is dead" was Pallant's news.
- **Ch XIX**: Pallant's burglary theory; "your clock in the hall might have been wrong" (Dora set watch by it 2 Aug, 9.30pm). Allen ill (letter from servant Emma). Dora tells Mrs Tice: "Lady Burville is my mother."
- **Ch XX**: Mrs Tice's story: Miss Treherne courted by Dr Scott (widower, flirt), Dargill, Carew. Carew married her; Carew jealous; learned Dargill would enter drawing-room by French window; Dr Scott came in his place (summoned by Laura) and was shot through the heart. Carew fled, never caught.
- **Ch XXI**: Allen explains: Edermont told him Carew killed his father; Allen threatened Edermont; Edermont shouted. Allen went to London, read *Morning Planet* file. Dora: Pallant not killer. "That secret is worth fifty thousand pounds and your life."
- **Ch XXII**: Meg: hall clock was one hour fast morning after murder (set ahead, so Joad's alibi at one would make murder at twelve). Dora searches Joad's cottage (key under water-butt); finds manuscript in fireplace: "The Confession of Julian Dargill, better known as Julian Edermont."
- **Ch XXIII**: Joad discovers loss, rages ("I know who stole it"). Joad to Canterbury to see Carver; heart attack at gate. Dora brings manuscript to Carver, then Allen.
- **Ch XXIV**: Manuscript (Dargill's voice): born Christchurch; friend John Mallison (ten yrs travel, later Pride). Laura Treherne courted by Dargill, Scott, Carew. Carew married her; ship *Silver Arrow* wrecked off Guinea; Dargill married Laura; Dora born; Carew returned; Dargill fled; Mallison took his name, went to America; Dargill became Edermont, bought Red House via Carver. Dora = Dargill's daughter, not Carew's; birth certificate with family lawyer in Lincoln's Inn Fields. Allen: "your father did not kill mine—and we can marry!"
- **Ch XXV**: Edermont had secretly funded Allen's education. Carver: Joad confessed to Carver (accessory after fact). Full account: Pallant sought letters; Edermont wrote Laura to come midnight 2 Aug, wrote Allen too; Joad intercepted letter at village post office; Joad hid in hall, altered clock; Laura gave letters, left; Mallison (Pride) came, quarrelled over cut pension, smashed Edermont with knobkerrie; Mallison threatened Joad; Mallison and Joad went to Joad's cottage for alibi. Mallison = Pride (John Mallison).
- **Ch XXVI**: Joad died of heart disease on his doorstep the night Pride was arrested (Meg testified re clock). Joad's will left £50,000 to Dora. Laura confessed to Sir John, was forgiven, remarried him. Pallant shot in San Francisco gambling house (fan-tan). Mallison confessed day before execution; executed. Dora to marry Allen in spring; live in Canterbury; Mrs Tice housekeeper. Carver: "Hear, hear!" (misogamist). THE END.

## BOOK 2: THE SPRING SONG (Forrest Reid, 1916, Edward Arnold, London)

Epigraph: Donne, "I am a little world made cunningly / Of elements, and an angelic sprite."

**Cast**
- **Griffith "Grif" Weston**: 13, sallow, dark eyes, sleepy-gentle, Perugino-like face; sleepwalker; sensitive to sounds; loves trees, music; devoted to Pouncer; visits Batts; sings.
- **Pouncer**: bulldog (orange/white, black nose, kinky tail), Grif's dog; "Bouncer" to Ann.
- **Barbara** (12, prim, yellow croquet ball, wants to be Angelina); **Ann** (10, fat, red hair, freckles, mouth open, loves Palmer, "Balmer"); **Jim** (9, sailor-suit, riddles, "Bun"); **Edward** (15, at school, fair, blue eyes, smokes, Angelina nickname, vain).
- **Miss Johnson**: governess, pince-nez, writing novel *Be True, Fond Heart* (Reginald, Angelina, Maud Vivien, Captain Victor De Lancy).
- **Canon Annesley** (grandpapa): clergyman, writing book on fairies, round velvet cap, *Golden Bough*, angry at circus cruelty.
- **Aunt Caroline Annesley**: tall, fair, smiling, letter-writer.
- **Palmer Dorset**: 15ish (six months older than Edward), red hair, freckled, small reddish-brown eyes, clever, inventor (writing device), detective fan (Sherlock Holmes, Raffles, Bunny), finger-tips-together pose; shoots George; later gets revolver from Doctor O'Neill.
- **Mr Clement Bradley** (Tennant; "Mr Bradley"): organist, Oxford man, silver hair, sly cat-eyes, ebony stick; killed a man (homicide), was in asylum, father's guarantee; now organist at Chillum; sees Grif as "playmate"; dies in burning church, tower leap.
- **Mr Drummond**: curate, smooth-faced, disapproving.
- **Captain Narcissus Batt, Miss Nancy Batt, Miss Jane Batt**: old pleasant family in red brick house with pond, cedars, terraces, garden door; **Billy (William Batt) Tremaine**, grandson, died ~4 yrs ago aged 14; flute; "Tremaine" grave by church wall (crest, Latin motto).
- **Doctor O'Neill**: bachelor 30–35, car, consulting-room; treats Grif; gives Palmer revolver.
- **Bridget, Hannah**: servants. **Johnnie**: boy who cleans knives and boots (bitten by Pouncer, "Daniel" game). **Robert**: coachman. **Meg**: no; **Emma**: none in Book 2.
- **George** ("Prairie Dick," circus rider, earring man, Lascar-like; steals Pouncer; shot in leg by Palmer).
- **Gian Peruzzi**: Italian organist who wrote the "Spring Song" tune (~200 yrs ago).

**Chronology**
- **Ch I** (June): train to canon's Glebe; Grif, Barbara, Ann, Jim, Miss Johnson, Pouncer; Aunt Caroline meets at station; Grif's strength and fever history; Pouncer splashes at water basin.
- **Ch II**: Walk down beech lane; Ann tired; meet Bradley (black clothes, ebony stick, "expecting important letters"). Ann/Grif dialogue on canon's book. Glebe: ivy, croquet lawn, wood behind wall. Grif chooses room by wood (swallow's nest); asks to sleep with Pouncer.
- **Ch III**: Croquet; Edward arrives with Palmer; "Angelina" nickname; cigarettes; Jim's riddle; dinner with canon (Euxine sea line); Miss Johnson's novel; canon Jim game.
- **Ch IV**: Night at window: wood-spirit song (verses "What is this coming..."). Grif thinks of Tobias, angel; flute heard.
- **Ch V**: Croquet tournament (draws: Edward/Barbara, Ann/Palmer, Jim/canon, Grif/Aunt Caroline, Miss Johnson/Drummond). Grif leaves into wood; iris stream; garden door; tortoiseshell butterfly; lady (unnamed here) with roses and cat; Captain Narcissus Batt; Miss Nancy, Miss Jane; lunch with raspberry wine; flute on cabinet "belongs to Billy—Billy Tremaine, my grandson."
- **Ch VI**: Church, Bradley plays; Grif sees vision of old city, procession, black bird; Bradley startled; Grif sings scale; Bradley: ghost (flute, Spring Song) seen "behind me" in church; "A Few More Years Shall Roll," Spohr's "Rose Softly Blooming." Grif loses Palmer's butterfly-net at Batts'.
- **Ch VII**: Grif late; supper; Mr Drummond and Robert searched; canon: Billy died ~4 yrs ago; father drowned at sea, mother died at birth. Miss Johnson: Grif "not perfectly truthful," Italian organ-grinder episode. Palmer's "Holmes" pose.
- **Ch VIII**: Rain. Miss Johnson sees naked boy on river (sixteen-ish), angry. Jim and Johnnie's Daniel-and-Lion game; Pouncer bites Johnnie. Palmer's tale of boy raising devil. Play *Be True Fond Heart* performed in back drawing-room (Edward as De Lancy, Palmer as Reginald, Ann Angelina, Jim/Barbara Maud; Mrs Ravenshawe's dress rips; liquorice wine bottle breaks; Mr Drummond attends). Grif says he'll apologize to Miss Johnson.
- **Ch IX**: Circus trip cancelled; Ann alone; man with earrings seen by Ann near house; Pouncer missing; Grif runs to town (butcher, public house), takes train without ticket; circus camp far; sleeps by stream until night.
- **Ch X**: Night: Pouncer barks; caravan; Grif frees circus dogs (bulldog, Great Dane, three terriers, spaniel); woman beats dogs with stick; circus boy pursues; Pouncer bites him; Grif sleeps in estate near a big white house.
- **Ch XI**: Ann plays Sunday school. Palmer borrows 15 shillings from Hannah and Edward's bicycle; takes Canon's life-preserver; revolver bought from saddler's second-hand. Palmer and Edward at tool-shed; George comes; Palmer shoots George in leg; George's excuses; Canon takes George into kitchen; Pouncer returned later; Doctor O'Neill ("I'd like a boy like that").
- **Ch XII**: Grif wakes at dawn by river; dragon-fly rescue; flute from rushes; Grif goes to a house, rings and lunches.
- **Ch XIII**: Motor-car home; Aunt Caroline's scolding; Grif to churchyard; Billy's grave ("William Batt Tremaine, aged fourteen"); Tobit reading; dragon-fly memory; Palmer runs from gate.
- **Ch XIV**: Bradley and Grif by Billy's grave: flute, Spring Song is Billy's last tune; "the soul does not die"; "danger from him." Grif promises secrecy.
- **Ch XV**: Palmer's treacle for moths; quarrel; Grif sleeps, sleepwalks at night to Batts' area; wakes in long wet grass by Pouncer; Palmer lets him in; Palmer says Bradley's real name Tennant; Grif faints.
- **Ch XVI**: Grif sends Jim with note to Bradley; Bradley visits; shadow story (man kills brother on bridge). Aunt Caroline returns.
- **Ch XVII**: O'Neill: Grif worse, "shock." Aunt Caroline sits up. Dream: china dogs, graveyard gate, shadow strangles Grif; Pouncer attacks shadow.
- **Ch XVIII**: Grif wakes; ill three days ("This is Wednesday night"); Pouncer back.
- **Ch XIX**: O'Neill and Palmer in Jonah's Bower; Palmer's theory (Bradley mad, Tennant, asylum); O'Neill and Palmer plan to search Bradley's lodgings.
- **Ch XX**: Miss Johnson's birthday; Palmer's "age trick" (34); fireworks; bonfire put out by canon; O'Neill's car summons Palmer.
- **Ch XXI**: O'Neill gives Palmer smaller revolver; search of Bradley's lodgings (signature "Clement Bradley Tennant"); Bradley returns; Palmer's silhouette remark; Bradley's grimace; Palmer's Jane-and-sovereigns story. Canon dismisses concern.
- **Ch XXII**: Johnnie: fire, Bradley playing organ. Church burns; Bradley on tower in crucifixion pose; dives; dies. Canon, Edward, Jim watch.
- **Ch XXIII**: O'Neill learns Bradley's history (homicide, asylum, false name); Aunt Caroline calls Palmer "callous," not good; O'Neill angry; Grif sinks ("the Spring Song sang in his ears").
- **Ch XXIV**: Late September; Grif visits Batts; Miss Nancy shows Billy's room (stamps, soldiers, boat, books, picture); Grif relieved; sleeps in Miss Nancy's arms. Last line: "But Grif slept on." THE END.
